content: 1. The metabolism of ethinylestradiol can be affected by the intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction necessitates caution and close monitoring when co-administered with other drugs that influence this pathway. 2. Amoxicillin may reduce the levels or effectiveness of ethinylestradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormonal contraceptives. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Antibiotics, including ampicillin, cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, and cefuroxime, may decrease the effectiveness of ethinylestradiol by disrupting the intestinal flora. This effect is specific to oral hormonal contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 4. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of norethindrone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Alternative contraceptive methods should be considered if available. 6. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of atogepant by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Atorvastatin may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels of axitinib and bendamustine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and reducing their clearance. Bendamustine is minimally metabolized by CYP1A2, and ethinylestradiol, as a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor, may increase its plasma concentrations. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Ethinylestradiol may increase caffeine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Clobazam, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives by decreasing norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 11. Ceritinib may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Chloramphenicol may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Cimetidine may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Ciprofloxacin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Clarithromycin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 16. Clindamycin may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of clonazepam by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing their serum concentrations. 18. Colesevelam decreases norethindrone levels by binding the drug in the gastrointestinal tract. Oral contraceptives containing norethindrone/ethinylestradiol should be administered at least 4 hours before colesevelam to avoid reduced absorption. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Crofelemer may increase norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. Caution and monitoring are advised. Crofelemer is minimally absorbed and unlikely to inhibit CYP3A4 systemically. 20. Ethinylestradiol may increase cyclosporine levels by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Dabrafenib may reduce the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 22. Danicopan may increase ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting BCRP substrates. Dose reduction of BCRP substrates should be considered. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Elagolix, a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the levels or effects of norethindrone and ethinylestradiol. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are advised during and after elagolix treatment. 24. Ethinylestradiol may increase eltrombopag levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Cobicistat is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious adverse events. 26. Encorafenib may increase or decrease ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting or inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. Encorafenib may also increase the concentration and toxicity of BCRP substrates. Dose adjustments of these substrates may be necessary. 27. Erythromycin and its derivatives (ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) may reduce ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Etravirine may reduce norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 29. Exenatide may impair the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by reducing glucose tolerance. It may also reduce the absorption of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. 30. Fedratinib may increase norethindrone and ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 31. Ethinylestradiol may increase finerenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Serum potassium should be monitored during initiation and dosage adjustments of finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Finerenone dosage adjustments may be necessary. 32. Fosamprenavir may variably affect norethindrone levels through an unspecified mechanism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 33. Ethinylestradiol may increase flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Increased adverse effects of flibanserin may occur if co-administered. Caution and monitoring are advised.
